info.title: Bugaboo API
info.description: The API of Bugaboo. The browser app uses exactly this API. Every error is application/problem+json with a stable code and a message key.

get.summary: The access keys of the person, a page at a time.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many items a page holds at most (default 50, at most 100).

200.description: The keys of the person, newest first.

post.summary: Creates an access key. The key is shown once. The password is asked again.

get.summary:
The projects the person may limit a key to: those they know about, by short name, a page at a
time.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many items a page holds at most (default 50, at most 100).

200.description: The projects the person may know about, by short name.

get.summary: How long a new access key lives in this organization.

200.description: The default and the longest time a key lives, in days.

delete.summary: Deletes an access key at once. A deleted key cannot come back.

parameters.name: access_key
parameters.description: The ID of the key.

get.summary:
How the server is doing: version, uptime, database, certificate and the check of the security
log. Needs the permission *See how the server is doing*.

The people, groups or roles that the form of a row for the whole organization offers, by
name, a page at a time. Needs the permission *Decide who has which role* for the whole
organization. Names only, never e-mail addresses.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many items a page holds at most (default 50, at most 100).

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: What to list: people (when left out), groups or roles.

schema.description: What kind of thing a choice is.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Words that every found name holds, without regard to capitals.

get.summary:
The rows of *Who has which role* for the whole organization, a page at a time. Needs the
permission *Decide who has which role* for the whole organization.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many items a page holds at most (default 50, at most 100).

200.description: The rows for the whole organization.

post.summary:
Gives a role to a person or a group for the whole organization. Needs the permission *Decide
who has which role* for the whole organization; nobody gives a role with more than they hold
themselves.

delete.summary:
Takes a row of *Who has which role* away. Needs the permission *Decide who has which role*
where the row is; nothing that would leave nobody who can manage roles.

parameters.name: assignment
parameters.description: The ID of the row.

delete.summary:
Puts a file into the trash (*Undo* takes it out again). The person who added it may, and whoever
may change issues.

parameters.name: attachment
parameters.description: The ID of the attachment.

204.description: The file is in the trash.

post.summary: Takes a file out of the trash (*Undo*).

parameters.name: attachment
parameters.description: The ID of the attachment.

200.description: The attachment, out of the trash.

get.summary: The open invitations, a page at a time. Needs the permission *Invite people*.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many items a page holds at most (default 50, at most 100).

200.description: The open invitations, newest first. Only invitations that are still open are listed.

post.summary: Creates an invitation. The link is shown once. Needs the permission *Invite people*.
Creates an account from an invitation link, and signs the person in.

200.description: The account was made and is signed in.

post.summary:
Shows which address an invitation is for. It is a `POST` so the secret is in the body, not in
an address that logs and browser history keep.

delete.summary: Takes an invitation back. Needs the permission *Invite people*.

parameters.name: invitation
parameters.description: The ID of the invitation.

get.summary: Who is signed in.

200.description: The signed-in person and what they may do for the whole organization.

post.summary: Signs in with a passkey alone.
Starts signing in with a passkey alone: the device offers its passkeys for this server.
Adds a passkey.

Starts adding a passkey. The password is typed again, so a stolen session cannot add a way
to sign in.
Removes a passkey. The password is typed again.

parameters.name: passkey
parameters.description: The ID of the passkey.

post.summary: Changes the password. Other sessions end and the session of the request gets a new secret.

200.description: Changed; new cookies come with it.

post.summary: Finishes signing in with a code from the code app or a backup code.

401.description: The code is wrong or was used already, or there is no half finished sign-in (auth.wrong-second-step-code, auth.not-signed-in).

post.summary: Finishes signing in with a passkey after the password.
Starts checking a passkey as the second step of signing in.

get.summary: The sessions of the signed-in person.

200.description: Where the person is signed in.

delete.summary: Ends every session of the person, the one of the request included ("sign out everywhere").
Ends one session of the person.

parameters.name: session
parameters.description: The ID of the session.

post.summary:
Creates the first administrator with the setup code, and signs them in. Setup is closed for
good afterwards.

200.description: The administrator was made and is signed in.

401.description: The setup code is wrong, or setup is over (auth.wrong-setup-code).

post.summary:
Signs in with e-mail address and password. An unknown address and a wrong password get the
same answer. When the person has a second step, the session can only finish it.

200.description: Signed in, or the second step is still to do.

401.description: The e-mail address or the password is wrong (auth.wrong-credentials).

post.summary: Ends the session of the request and clears both cookies.

Asks for an account without an invitation, when an administrator allows it and e-mail is on.
Nothing is made yet: the answer is `202` for every address, and a link goes to the address
(24 hours, once) that opens the invitation page.

202.description: An e-mail goes to the address, the same answer for every address.

403.description: Signing up is not possible here (auth.sign-up-refused): it is off, the domain is not listed, or e-mail is off.

get.summary: Who may sign up on their own. Needs the permission *Change organization settings*.

put.summary: Changes who may sign up on their own. Needs the permission *Change organization settings*.

get.summary: Whether setup is open and whether people may sign up. Open to everyone.

200.description: What the app needs before anybody signs in.

get.summary: How the second step is set up.

200.description: The second step of the person.

post.summary: Creates new backup codes; the old ones stop working. The password is typed again.

Starts setting up the code app. It is not asked for until the first code is confirmed. The
password is typed again, so a stolen session cannot add a way to sign in.
Finishes setting up the code app with its first code, and makes the backup codes.

200.description: Set up; the backup codes are shown once.

post.summary: Switches the code app off. The password is typed again.

get.summary:
The people to choose from for *Check access*, a page at a time, by name. A person who cannot
see names there is listed nobody. Needs the permission *Check what other people can do, and
why* in the place.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many items a page holds at most (default 50, at most 100).

parameters.name: project
parameters.description:
The ID of the project. Without it the answer is about the whole organization: the level
each role has of its own.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Words that every found name holds, in any order; left out or empty, everybody is listed.

get.summary:
What a person can do in a project, or in the whole organization when no project is named:
every permission with *yes* or *no*, every field with its level and how the person sees
people, each with the reasons. With an issue type, the field levels are those for issues of that
type; `differs_by_type` says whether they differ by type at all. Needs the permission *Check what other people can do, and why*
in the place.

parameters.name: person
parameters.description: The ID of the person to check.

parameters.name: project
parameters.description:
The ID of the project. Without it the answer is about the whole organization: the level
each role has of its own.

parameters.name: issue_type
parameters.description:
The ID of an issue type: the levels that count for issues of this type.
Without it the answer is about all issue types.

200.description: What the person can do, and why.

parameters.name: comment
parameters.description: The ID of the comment.

200.description: The comment as it is now.

delete.summary:
Puts a comment into the trash (*Undo* takes it out again). The author may, and whoever may
change issues.

parameters.name: comment
parameters.description: The ID of the comment.

204.description: The comment is in the trash.

post.summary: Takes a comment out of the trash (*Undo*).

parameters.name: comment
parameters.description: The ID of the comment.

200.description: The comment, out of the trash.

get.summary:
Every text a comment had, the current one last, a page at a time. Whoever may see the comment
may see its earlier texts.

parameters.name: comment
parameters.description: The ID of the comment.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many items a page holds at most (default 50, at most 100).

get.summary:
The hosts that images in text may come from (the setting `content.image-hosts`), for the preview
of the editor. Every signed-in person may read them: they are in the content security policy
that every page carries. The list is split here once; the browser never splits it again.
The draft of the person for a target: theirs, and nobody else's.

parameters.name: record_kind
parameters.description: The kind of record.

parameters.name: record_id
parameters.description: The ID of the record, for a draft of a part of a record.

parameters.name: part
parameters.description: Which long text of the record, for a draft of a part of a record.

parameters.name: project
parameters.description: The project, for a draft of a new record.

put.summary:
Keeps a text as the draft of the person, in place of the older one for the same target. Only the
person can read it, until it is saved, thrown away, or 30 days old.

200.description: The draft as it is kept.

post.summary: Throws the draft of the person away (*Throw away*).

get.summary:
Says whether somebody is editing a long text, and who, without taking the lock: the box asks
when it opens, so a person who comes second is told before the first key.

parameters.name: record_kind
parameters.description: The kind of record.

parameters.name: record_id
parameters.description: The ID of the record.

parameters.name: part
parameters.description: Which long text of the record, like `description`.

post.summary:
Takes the lock on a long text, on the first keystroke, or says who is editing it. The lock is a
lease of a minute that the heartbeat renews; closing the page lets it run out.

200.description: The editor has the lock, or somebody else is editing.

post.summary:
Asks the person who is editing to finish (*Ask … to finish*). They read it at their next
heartbeat.

Takes the editing over (*Edit anyway*). Needs the permission *Take over text somebody else is
editing*. The person who was editing keeps their text as their draft and reads at their next
heartbeat that it was taken over.

200.description: The editor has the lock now.

post.summary: Lets go of a lock: the text was saved, or the editor was closed.

Releases a lock that is stuck, whoever holds it. Needs the permission *Take over text somebody
else is editing*; it is written to the security log.

Renews the lease of a lock, keeps the text so far as the draft of the person (also when the lock
is gone), and hands over what others did since the last heartbeat: somebody asked to finish, or
took the editing over.

200.description: Whether the editor still has the lock, and the notes for it.

get.summary:
Which level every role has for every field, for the whole organization or for one project,
and where each level was set. Needs the permission *Decide which fields and which people
information each role sees*.

parameters.name: project
parameters.description:
The ID of the project. Without it the answer is about the whole organization: the level
each role has of its own.

parameters.name: issue_type
parameters.description:
The ID of an issue type: the levels that count for issues of this type.
Without it the answer is about all issue types.

put.summary:
Sets the level of a field for a role, for the whole organization (the role's own level) or for
one project and its sub-projects; `null` takes a project's setting away. A level above the
person's own is refused. Needs the permission *Decide which fields and which people
information each role sees* in the place.

parameters.name: role
parameters.description: The ID of the role.

parameters.name: field
parameters.description: The key of the field: its word, or the ID of an own field.

parameters.name: project
parameters.description:
The ID of the project. Without it the answer is about the whole organization: the level
each role has of its own.

parameters.name: issue_type
parameters.description:
The ID of an issue type: the levels that count for issues of this type.
Without it the answer is about all issue types.

get.summary: The kinds of information a field can hold, with what each kind allows.
The own fields the person sees, for the organization or for one project.

parameters.name: applies_to
parameters.description: Only fields for this kind of item.

parameters.name: project
parameters.description: Only the fields used in this project (its ID or short name).

parameters.name: retired
parameters.description: Also the retired fields.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many items a page holds at most (default 50, at most 100).

200.description: The fields, a page at a time.

post.summary: Creates an own field. Needs the permission *Manage fields*.

get.summary: One own field the person sees.

parameters.name: field
parameters.description: The ID of the field.

patch.summary:
Changes an own field, or retires it (or offers it again). Needs the permission *Manage
fields*.

parameters.name: field
parameters.description: The ID of the field.

200.description: The field as it is now.

post.summary: Adds a choice to a *Pick one* or *Pick several* field. Needs the permission *Manage fields*.

parameters.name: field
parameters.description: The ID of the field.

200.description: The field as it is now.

put.summary: Puts the choices of a field in a new order. Needs the permission *Manage fields*.

parameters.name: field
parameters.description: The ID of the field.

200.description: The field as it is now.

patch.summary:
Changes the name, color or icon of a choice, or retires it. Needs the permission *Manage
fields*.

parameters.name: field
parameters.description: The ID of the field.

parameters.name: choice
parameters.description: The ID of the choice.

200.description: The field as it is now.

post.summary:
Moves every value of a choice to another choice and retires the first (*Combine with another
choice*). Every item it touches gets a record in its history. Needs the permission *Manage
fields*.

parameters.name: field
parameters.description: The ID of the field.

parameters.name: choice
parameters.description: The ID of the choice that goes away.

200.description: The field as it is now.

get.summary: Where an own field is used now. Needs the permission *Manage fields*.

parameters.name: field
parameters.description: The ID of the field.

get.summary:
Downloads a file, or shows its preview, through a signed link: one made for this person, good
for five minutes. The use case judges again that the person sees the issue and the comment, so
a link that is passed on or kept after access ended opens nothing. The file is sent as an
attachment with `nosniff` and a policy that allows nothing; SVG and HTML are only downloaded.

parameters.name: file
parameters.description: The signed address of a file, as the list of files gives it.

200.description: The bytes of the file, or the PNG of its preview.

get.summary:
The groups, by name, a page at a time. Needs the permission *Create, rename and delete groups
and change who is in them*.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many items a page holds at most (default 50, at most 100).

post.summary: Creates a group. Needs the permission *Create, rename and delete groups and change who is in them*.

get.summary:
One group, with what it is used for. Needs the permission *Create, rename and delete groups and
change who is in them*.

parameters.name: group
parameters.description: The ID of the group.

delete.summary:
Deletes a group, with its members and the rows that give it a role. Needs the permission
*Create, rename and delete groups and change who is in them*, and, where the group has *No
access*, *Decide who has which role* there.

parameters.name: group
parameters.description: The ID of the group.

patch.summary:
Renames a group. Needs the permission *Create, rename and delete groups and change who is in
them*.

parameters.name: group
parameters.description: The ID of the group.

200.description: The group as it is now.

get.summary:
The people that can be put into a group, by name, a page at a time; those who are in it
already say so. Needs the permission *Create, rename and delete groups and change who is in
them*. Names only, never e-mail addresses.

parameters.name: group
parameters.description: The ID of the group.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many items a page holds at most (default 50, at most 100).

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Words that every found name holds, without regard to capitals.

get.summary:
The people in a group, a page at a time. Needs the permission *Create, rename and delete groups
and change who is in them*.

parameters.name: group
parameters.description: The ID of the group.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many items a page holds at most (default 50, at most 100).

put.summary:
Puts a person into a group. Needs the permission *Create, rename and delete groups and change
who is in them*; nobody puts somebody into a group that has a role with more than they hold
themselves.

parameters.name: group
parameters.description: The ID of the group.

parameters.name: person
parameters.description: The ID of the person.

204.description: The person is in the group.

delete.summary:
Takes a person out of a group. Needs the permission *Create, rename and delete groups and change
who is in them*, and, where the group has *No access*, *Decide who has which role* there.

parameters.name: group
parameters.description: The ID of the group.

parameters.name: person
parameters.description: The ID of the person.

204.description: The person is not in the group.

get.summary:
The issue types in the order they are offered in, a page at a time, retired ones too. Open to
everybody who is signed in. With `project`, each type can say whether that project offers it.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many items a page holds at most (default 50, at most 100).

parameters.name: project
parameters.description: The ID or short name of a project.

post.summary:
Creates an issue type for the whole organization or in a project. Needs the permission *Manage
issue types, kinds of relation and layouts* where it is made.

patch.summary:
Changes the name or the icon of an issue type, or retires it (or offers it again). Needs the
permission *Manage issue types, kinds of relation and layouts* where the type was made.

parameters.name: issue_type
parameters.description: The ID of the issue type.

200.description: The issue type as it is now.

get.summary:
Where an issue type is offered: the rows that say so, a page at a time. Open to everybody who is
signed in.

parameters.name: issue_type
parameters.description: The ID of the issue type.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many items a page holds at most (default 50, at most 100).

put.summary:
Changes where an issue type is offered: all the places together or none. Each place is judged on
its own: it needs the permission *Manage issue types, kinds of relation and layouts* there.

parameters.name: issue_type
parameters.description: The ID of the issue type.

200.description: Every row, and the version of the type.

get.summary:
One issue by its readable ID (an old one too; the answer holds the current one) or its
internal ID, with what the person may do with it. Needs the permission *See every issue of the
project*, or the issue is one the person reported.

parameters.name: issue
parameters.description: The readable ID (WEB-142) or the internal ID of the issue.

delete.summary:
Puts an issue into the trash. Needs the permission *Delete issues into the trash*. *Undo*
takes it out again.

parameters.name: issue
parameters.description: The readable ID (WEB-142) or the internal ID of the issue.

204.description: The issue is in the trash.

patch.summary:
Changes the fields of an issue. Needs the permission *Change anybody's issues*, or *Change the
issues they reported* on an issue the person reported; each field must be one the person may
change.

parameters.name: issue
parameters.description: The readable ID (WEB-142) or the internal ID of the issue.

200.description: The issue as it is now.

post.summary: Writes a comment under an issue. Needs the permission *Comment* and the right to see the issue.

parameters.name: issue
parameters.description: The readable ID (WEB-142) or the internal ID of the issue.

put.summary:
Saves the description of an issue under the edit lock the person holds, on the version they
started from. A refused save (the lock is gone, somebody took the editing over, the issue
changed) keeps the text as the draft of the person. Needs the permission *Change anybody's
issues*, or *Change the issues they reported* on an issue the person reported, and the right
to change the description.

parameters.name: issue
parameters.description: The readable ID (WEB-142) or the internal ID of the issue.

200.description: The issue as it is now.

put.summary:
Saves the long text of an own field of an issue, under the edit lock of the person. Needs the
right to change the issue and the field; a lock that ran out, a take-over or a change made
meanwhile keeps the text as the person's draft.

parameters.name: issue
parameters.description: The readable ID (WEB-142) or the internal ID of the issue.

parameters.name: field
parameters.description: The ID of the long text field.

200.description: The issue as it is now.

get.summary: What the reader may add to the issue, and the most bytes one file may have in its project.

parameters.name: issue
parameters.description: The readable ID (WEB-142) or the internal ID of the issue.

get.summary:
The files of an issue and of the comments under it, oldest first. Each has the signed links of
the file and of its preview for the reader.

parameters.name: issue
parameters.description: The readable ID (WEB-142) or the internal ID of the issue.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many items a page holds at most (default 50, at most 100).

get.summary: Whether the person follows the issue (*Follow* or *Following*).

parameters.name: issue
parameters.description: The readable ID (WEB-142) or the internal ID of the issue.

put.summary: Creates the person a follower of the issue. Following it already changes nothing.

parameters.name: issue
parameters.description: The readable ID (WEB-142) or the internal ID of the issue.

delete.summary: Takes the person out of the followers of the issue. Not following changes nothing.

parameters.name: issue
parameters.description: The readable ID (WEB-142) or the internal ID of the issue.

204.description: The person does not follow the issue.

get.summary: Who follows an issue, a page at a time, each as the kind *Followers* says for the reader.

parameters.name: issue
parameters.description: The readable ID (WEB-142) or the internal ID of the issue.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many items a page holds at most (default 50, at most 100).

get.summary:
The history of an issue, newest first, a page at a time: the comments and the changes, in three
tabs. A change to a field the person may not see is not in it. A row's changes stay together, so
a page may hold a few items more than `limit`.

parameters.name: issue
parameters.description: The readable ID (WEB-142) or the internal ID of the issue.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many items a page holds at most (default 50, at most 100).

parameters.name: tab
parameters.description: Everything (the default), only the comments, or only the changes.

post.summary:
Puts a label on an issue. In a *Pick one* group the label takes the place of the one the issue
has from that group.

parameters.name: issue
parameters.description: The readable ID (WEB-142) or the internal ID of the issue.

200.description: The tags and labels of the issue now.

get.summary: The tags and labels of an issue and what the person may do with them.

parameters.name: issue
parameters.description: The readable ID (WEB-142) or the internal ID of the issue.

200.description: The tags and labels of the issue.

delete.summary: Takes a label off an issue.

parameters.name: issue
parameters.description: The readable ID (WEB-142) or the internal ID of the issue.

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: The ID of the label.

200.description: The tags and labels of the issue now.

get.summary:
What the writer of a comment under this issue may name after `@`: people and groups for someone
who sees names, groups and roles for someone who sees roles only, nobody for someone who sees no
people. Needs the permission *Comment*.

parameters.name: issue
parameters.description: The readable ID (WEB-142) or the internal ID of the issue.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many items a page holds at most (default 50, at most 100).

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: The start of a name; every choice when left out.

post.summary:
Moves an issue into another project, on the version the person looked at. The issue gets a
readable ID of that project and the old one keeps working. It moves only where the project
offers its issue type, uses every own field it has a value in and allows its tags. Needs the
permission *Move issues* in both projects.

parameters.name: issue
parameters.description: The readable ID (WEB-142) or the internal ID of the issue.

200.description: The issue, in its new project.

put.summary:
Puts an issue under another one, or takes it out from under its parent. Needs the right to
change both issues. No issue sits under itself or under one of its own sub-issues.

parameters.name: issue
parameters.description: The readable ID (WEB-142) or the internal ID of the sub-issue.

get.summary:
The issues related to an issue, whose other end the person may see, a page at a time, by kind
and then oldest first. Each relation reads in the words of this issue's end.

parameters.name: issue
parameters.description: The readable ID (WEB-142) or the internal ID of the issue.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many items a page holds at most (default 50, at most 100).

get.summary:
How an issue stands among the others: the issue it sits under and the progress of its
sub-issues. The lists are `sub-issues` and `related-issues`.

parameters.name: issue
parameters.description: The readable ID (WEB-142) or the internal ID of the issue.

post.summary:
Adds a relation between this issue and another. Needs the right to change this issue and to see
the other. The relation shows on both issues, each in its own words.

parameters.name: issue
parameters.description: The readable ID (WEB-142) or the internal ID of the issue.

200.description: The relation as this issue reads it.

post.summary:
Takes an issue out of the trash (*Undo*). Needs the permission *Delete issues into the
trash*.

parameters.name: issue
parameters.description: The readable ID (WEB-142) or the internal ID of the issue.

200.description: The issue, out of the trash.

get.summary:
*Try it*: the status changes a person would get on an issue, and why not the others. Needs the
permission *Manage workflows* in the project of the issue.

parameters.name: issue
parameters.description: The readable ID (WEB-142) or the internal ID of the issue.

parameters.name: person
parameters.description: The ID of the person.

200.description: The status changes and the answer for each.

get.summary:
The sub-issues of an issue that the person may see, a page at a time, in the order they were
put there.

parameters.name: issue
parameters.description: The readable ID (WEB-142) or the internal ID of the issue.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many items a page holds at most (default 50, at most 100).

post.summary:
Puts a tag on an issue by its name. A name nobody used makes the tag. Needs the right to change
the issue and its field *Tags*.

parameters.name: issue
parameters.description: The readable ID (WEB-142) or the internal ID of the issue.

200.description: The tags and labels of the issue now.

delete.summary: Takes a tag off an issue.

parameters.name: issue
parameters.description: The readable ID (WEB-142) or the internal ID of the issue.

parameters.name: tag
parameters.description: The ID of the tag.

200.description: The tags and labels of the issue now.

post.summary:
Starts an upload of a file to an issue, or to a comment under it. Needs the right to change the
issue (a Guest: an issue they reported), or, for a comment, to have written it. A file that is
too big for the project or of a type the organization never accepts is refused here, before
any part is sent.

parameters.name: issue

own.description: Whether this level has a value of its own, which *Reset to default* takes away.

version.description:
In a person's own settings: counts up with every change of the value of their own, `0`
while there is none. A change sends back the version that was looked at.

SettingFormat.description: What kind of text a text setting holds.

SettingLevel.description: Where a setting can be set.

SettingSourceKind.description: Where the value that counts comes from.

SettingsBody.description: The settings of a topic, in the order of the registry.

SetupBody.description: The first administrator, with the setup code.

code.description: The setup code the server printed.

email.description: The e-mail address of the administrator.

ShareBody.description: The group or the project to share with.

id.description: The ID of the group or the project.

ShareChoiceItem.description: A group or a project the person may share with.

id.description: The ID of the group or the project.

short_name.description: The short name of a project.

ShareKind.description: What a saved search is shared with: a group or a project.

ShareRef.description: A group or a project a saved search is shared with.

id.description: The ID of the group or the project.

name.description: Its name; left out for a project the person may not know.

short_name.description: The short name of a project the person may know.

SignInBody.description: What a person types to sign in.

SignUpAnswer.description: What signing up comes to: the same for every address.

check_your_mail.description:
Always `true`: an e-mail goes to the address. For an address with no account it holds a link
to the invitation page, where the person chooses a name and a password; for an address with
one it says so. Nothing is made yet, and the answer does not tell which of the two it is.

SignUpPolicyBody.description: Who may sign up on their own.

domains.description: The e-mail domains that may sign up. Empty: every domain, while signing up is on.

enabled.description: Whether signing up without an invitation is on.

version.description:
Counts up with every change. A change is made on the version that was looked at; the
policy has version 0 until it is changed the first time.

SignedInBody.description: The answer to signing in. The cookies come with it.

oneOf.description:
Who signed in. Left out while the second step is still to do: a password alone shows
nothing about the person.

When present, the password was right but the person still has to finish with one of
these ways before anything else opens.

SkipReason.description: Why an issue of the selection is left alone.

SlotBody.description: The layout or the workflow set at exactly the place that was asked about.

id.description: The ID of the layout or workflow, which the edit lock is about.

version.description: Counts up with every change. A change is made on the version that was looked at.

SourceBody.description: Where the value that counts comes from.

oneOf.description: For a value from a project: which one. Missing when the person cannot see the project.

StandingBody.description: What a person has in one project.

held_back.description: A *No access* holds the person back there.

roles.description: The names of their roles there, in the order of roles.

comment.description: The comment the file is for; left out for a file of the issue itself.

name.description: The name of the file as the device has it. A path is cut off.

StatusChangeRef.description: A status change the reader may make on an issue now.

needs.description:
The fields the change still needs before it can be made (*Must be filled in* fields that
are empty, and *Ask for* fields), each with the kind of input it needs. Empty when it needs
none.

StatusDraftBody.description: A status as the editor sends it.

key.description:
The key of a status the workflow has. Left out for a new status, which gets a key made from
its name; a status change names a new status by its name.

status_group.description: The status group it belongs to.

StatusMoveBody.description: Where the issues of a dropped status go.

from.description: The key of the status that is dropped.

to.description: The status of the new workflow the issues go to: its key, or its name when it is new.

StatusRef.description: A status as it is shown: the browser keeps no list of statuses, it shows what the server sends.

key.description: The key, which never changes: it is what a request names a status by.

status_group.description: The status group it belongs to.

StatusRulesBody.description: The rules of a status change.

ask_for.description: *Ask for*: the keys of the fields shown in a small form during the change.

must_fill.description: *Must be filled in*: the keys of the fields that need a value first.

StatusValue.description: The only value a status can have today.

TagItem.description: A tag as the people who look after tags see it: the fields that can be asked for.

oneOf.description: Its color, as a category token of the theme.

projects.description: The projects it is limited to, as far as the person sees them.

version.description: Counts up with every change. A change is made on the version that was looked at.

whole_organization.description: Whether it is for every project.

TagRefBody.description: A tag as a small reference: what a chip needs.

color.description: Its color, as a category token of the theme.

TagSuggestionsBody.description: The tags to offer while a person types.

TakeLockBody.description: Which thing a person wants the lock on, and from which open editor.

editor_id.description: The open editor (a tab): an ID the browser makes when the editor opens.

target.description: The thing that is going to be edited.

expires_at.description: When the lock runs out if no heartbeat renews it.

heartbeat_seconds.description: How often to send a heartbeat, in seconds.

lease_seconds.description: How long a lease lasts, in seconds.

lock_token.description: The lock token to save with and to send with every heartbeat.

Topic.description: What a group of permissions is about.

changes.description: The status changes from there, each with the answer for the person.

status.description: The status the issue is in.

TriedChangeBody.description: One status change *Try it* looked at.

oneOf.description: The person may make it.
The person may make it once these fields have a value.
The person may not make it.

field.description: The key of the field it is about, when the person who tries may see it too.

TriedVerdictBody.description: What the judge says about one status change.

TwoStepBody.description: How the second step of a person is set up.

backup_codes_left.description: How many backup codes are left.

code_app.description: Whether a code app is set up.

passkeys.description:
The passkeys. A person has at most 20, so the list is not paged: it has a hard cap, and
`truncated` says when the cap cut it off.

truncated.description: There are more passkeys than the list holds.

UnreadBody.description: How many notifications the person has not read.

unread.description: The number, at most 100: only what the person may still see is counted.

UploadItem.description: An upload that is going on.

offset.description: Where the next part starts: the bytes the server has.

part_bytes.description: The most bytes one part may have.

size.description: The size the file will have.

issue_type.description: The issue type; leave it out for all types.

project.description: The project, by its ID or its short name; leave it out for the whole organization.

workflow.description:
The ID of the workflow the place uses from now on. Leave it out (or `null`) for the place to
follow its parent again.

oneOf.description: Yes or no.
A whole number.
Text, or one choice from a list written as text.

ValueBody.description: What a setting holds: yes or no, a whole number, or text.

VersionsBody.description: The versions of the records asked about, in the order asked.

items.description: One entry for each record asked about.

ViewKind.description: The kind of view a saved search is shown as. Other kinds come with their views.

to.description: The ID of the project it would go into; `null` for the top level.

WhoBody.description: Whom a row is for: name a person or a group, not both.

WhoCanBody.description:
*Who can do it*: the people who may make a status change. Naming nobody means everybody who may
change the issue; a rule never gives a right *Change anybody's issues* does not.

assigned.description: The people the issue is assigned to.

reported_by.description: The person who reported the issue.

WhoMayChangeBody.description: The roles that may change a field.

roles.description: The roles somebody holds in the project that may change the field.

roles_hidden.description: The reader is not shown the people of the project, so no role is named.

WordBody.description:
A word of the vocabulary with the message that names it: a kind of people information
or a level.

code.description: The word, as it stands in the API (`cost-center`, `can-see`).

message_key.description: The key of the message that names it.

WorkflowEditorBody.description: What the editor shows for a place.

fields.description: The fields the rules can name.

groups.description: The groups *Who can do it* can name.

oneOf.description: Where the workflow that counts is set, when it is another place.
The issue type of the place; none for all types.
The project of the place; none for the whole organization.

roles.description: The roles *Who can do it* can name.

oneOf.description:
The workflow set at this place. Without it the place uses the workflow it inherits (or the
starting workflow), and *Create* makes one.

accessKey.description: An access key from My settings, sent as `Authorization: Bearer bb_…`. It can do at most what its owner can do at the moment of the request, and nothing on the owner's own sign-in data.

ETag.description: A tag for this answer. Send it back as `If-None-Match` to get `304` when nothing changed.

RetryAfter.description: Seconds to wait before trying again.

Fields.name: fields
Fields.description: The fields each item holds, separated by commas. The answer schema names every field that can be asked for; when this is left out the route's own small default is used.

Cursor.name: cursor
Cursor.description: Where the page starts: the `next_cursor` of the page before.

NotModified.description: Nothing changed since the `ETag` that `If-None-Match` named. No body.

BadListRequest.description: The request is not valid: a cursor that is not one of this list, or a name in `fields` that does not exist (request.bad-cursor, request.unknown-field).

TooManyRequests.description: Too many tries. Please wait a little and try again. (rate-limit.exceeded)

InternalError.description: Something went wrong on our side. Nothing you did caused this. (server.internal)

Unavailable.description: Bugaboo is not available right now. Please try again in a moment. (server.unavailable)

BadRequest.description: The request is not valid (request.invalid, auth.password-too-short, auth.password-breached, auth.invitation-invalid, auth.passkey-rejected).

TooLarge.description: That is too big to send. (request.too-large)

Conflict.description: Something stands in the way of the change: a name that is taken, a change somebody made first, or a rule about moving projects (name.taken, edit.version-changed, project.move-lifts-no-access, project.move-into-itself, project.too-deep, project.preview-changed).

UploadPartConflict.description: The part does not start where the file stands, or the upload is not complete yet (file.wrong-part, file.incomplete).

FileTooBig.description: The file is bigger than the project allows, or the part is bigger than a part may be (file.too-big, request.too-large).

FileTypeBlocked.description: The organization does not accept this type of file (file.type-blocked).
